tasks.title: JSON todo store with unit tests
tasks.description: Create src/store.js, the persistence layer. It owns the on-disk format of ~/.todos.json — a JSON array of `{ id, text, done }` objects — and every read/write goes through functions that take the file path explicitly, so tests can point them at a scratch file and never touch a real home directory. The CLI task builds on top of this and must not re-implement any of it.

existing test style to mirror: node:test with node:assert/strict
confirms "type": "module" so src/store.js can use import syntax

edits.change: Create an ES module (no semicolons, named exports, matching src/greeting.js) that imports `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:os` and `randomUUID` from `node:crypto`, and exports exactly: `storePath(env = process.env)`, `loadTodos(file)`, `saveTodos(file, todos)`, `addTodo(file, text)`, `markDone(file, id)` and `removeTodo(file, id)`, implemented exactly as written in contract `store-api`. `addTodo` must append at the end of the array and return the new todo; `markDone` and `removeTodo` throw `No todo with id <id>` for an unknown id.

Create an ESM test file using `import { test } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, `import fs from 'node:fs'`, `import os from 'node:os'`, `import path from 'node:path'` plus `import { storePath, loadTodos, saveTodos, addTodo, markDone, removeTodo } from '../src/store.js'`. Every test creates its own scratch directory with `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'todo-store-'))` and passes `<scratch>/todos.json` to the store functions, so no test reads or writes a real home directory. Write these tests: (1) `storePath` resolves to `path.join(env.HOME, '.todos.json')` for a fake env `{ HOME: '/home/ada' }`, and falls back to `os.homedir()` when that object has no HOME; (2) `loadTodos` returns `[]` for a path that does not exist; (3) `addTodo` writes a file that parses to `[{ id: <string>, text: 'buy milk', done: false }]`, and a second `addTodo` appends without disturbing the first and produces a different id; (4) `markDone` sets `done` to true for the matching id and throws `/No todo with id/` for an unknown id; (5) `removeTodo` leaves the remaining todos in their original order and throws `/No todo with id/` for an unknown id; (6) `loadTodos` throws `Error: Corrupt todo store at` when the file contains `not json`, and also when it contains a JSON object rather than an array; (7) a `saveTodos` then `loadTodos` round trip returns deep-equal data.

tasks.title: Argument parsing and command rendering with tests
tasks.description: Create src/cli.js: the pure argument-parsing layer plus the command dispatcher. It contains no filesystem access of its own — every command delegates to src/store.js — and never touches console, so tests can drive it entirely in-process by passing a fake `io` object and a fake `env`.

context.reason: the six functions this module calls and the exact errors they throw
node:test style and scratch-dir pattern to mirror
existing module style: ESM, named exports, no semicolons

edits.change: Create an ES module (no semicolons, named exports) exporting `parseArgs(argv, env = process.env)` and `runCommand(argv, io = { out: console.log, err: console.error }, env = process.env)`, implemented exactly as written in contracts `cli-api` and `line-formats`, and import `storePath`, `loadTodos`, `addTodo`, `markDone`, `removeTodo` from './store.js'. `parseArgs` slices `argv.slice(2)` (argv[0]/argv[1] are node and the script), reads the command from index 2, sets `pending: true` only for `list` when `argv[3] === '--pending'`, collects `rest = argv.slice(3)` for the other commands, and sets `error` for: an empty argv, an unknown command (`Unknown command: <cmd>`), `add` with no text (`Usage: todo add <text>`), `done`/`remove` without an id (`Usage: todo <cmd> <id>`), and `list` with any argument other than `--pending`. `list` loads with `loadTodos(storePath(env))`, filters to `!t.done` when `pending` is set, prints the single line `No todos.` when nothing is visible, and otherwise prints `[ ] ${t.id} ${t.text}` for pending and `[x] ${t.id} ${t.text}` for finished todos. `add` calls `addTodo(storePath(env), rest.join(' '))` and prints `Added ${todo.id} ${todo.text}`; `done` calls `markDone(storePath(env), id)` and prints `Done ${id}`; `remove` calls `removeTodo(storePath(env), id)` and prints `Removed ${id}`. Print the help block for `help`, `--help` and an empty argv, listing exactly these lines: `Usage: todo <command>`, `  add <text>    Add a todo`, `  list [--pending]  List todos (done ones are marked with [x])`, `  done <id>      Mark a todo as done`, `  remove <id>    Delete a todo`, `Todos are stored in ${storePath(env)}`, and a blank line. Every user-visible byte must go through `io.out` / `io.err` — do not call `console` or write to `process.stdout` directly. Wrap the dispatch in try/catch and on a thrown Error write `Error: ${err.message}\n` to `io.err` and return 1; return 0 otherwise.

Create an ESM test file using `import { test } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, `import fs from 'node:fs'`, `import os from 'node:os'`, `import path from 'node:path'` and `import { parseArgs, runCommand } from '../src/cli.js'`. Every test creates a fake home directory with `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'todo-cli-'))` and passes it as `env = { HOME: fakeHome }`, capturing output with a fake `io` such as `{ out: (s) => outLines.push(s), err: (s) => errLines.push(s) }` — never the real console, so the suite stays silent. Write these tests: (1) parseArgs: `['node','todo','add','buy','milk']` gives command 'add' and text 'buy milk'; `['node','todo','list','--pending']` gives command 'list' with pending true; `['node','todo','done','abc']` gives command 'done' with id 'abc'; `['node','todo']`, `['node','todo','bogus']`, `['node','todo','add']` and `['node','todo','list','--nope']` each return a defined `error`. (2) add then list: exit code 0 and the list output contains `[ ] ` plus the added text; a second `add` call yields a second, different id in the list. (3) list marks finished todos: add two, `done` the first id, then `list` shows a line starting with `[x] <id>` for it and `[ ] ` for the other. (4) `list --pending` hides finished todos: after `done` on the only todo it prints exactly `No todos.`. (5) `done` prints `Done <id>` and `remove` prints `Removed <id>` and drops only the requested todo. (6) error handling: `done` with an unknown id writes a line matching `/^Error: No todo with id/` to the captured stderr and returns exit code 1; bare `todo` returns 0 and its captured stdout contains `Usage: todo <command>`.

It must contain no other logic and must not read from stdin, so the process exits naturally with the code runCommand returned.

Create an ESM test file using `import { test } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, `import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'`, `import fs from 'node:fs'`, `import os from 'node:os'` and `import path from 'node:path'`. contracts.statement: src/store.js exports exactly these named functions (all synchronous, all taking the store file path as their first argument so tests never touch a real home directory): `storePath(env = process.env)` returns `path.join(env.HOME ?? env.USERPROFILE ?? os.homedir(), '.todos.json')`; `loadTodos(file)` returns `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'))`, returns `[]` when the file does not exist, throws `new Error('Corrupt todo store at ' + file)` when the parsed JSON is not an array, and otherwise returns the parsed array unchanged; `saveTodos(file, todos)` calls `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(file), { recursive: true })` then writes `JSON.stringify(todos, null, 2) + '\n'`; `addTodo(file, text)` appends `{ id, text, done: false }` at the end of the array where `id` is `randomUUID()` from node:crypto and returns the new todo; `markDone(file, id)` sets `done: true` on the first todo whose `id` strictly equals `id` and throws `new Error('No todo with id ' + id)` when there is none; `removeTodo(file, id)` splices out the first todo whose `id` strictly equals `id` and throws `new Error('No todo with id ' + id)` when there is none. Every mutating function reads, mutates a plain array and writes it back through `saveTodos`.

src/cli.js exports `parseArgs(argv, env = process.env)` (pure: never reads or writes the filesystem) and `runCommand(argv, io = { out: console.log, err: console.error }, env = process.env)` which returns the process exit code 0 or 1. `parseArgs` returns `{ command: 'add'|'list'|'done'|'remove'|'help', text: string|undefined, id: string|undefined, pending: boolean, error: string|undefined }`: argv is sliced with `argv.slice(2)`, the command is argv[2], `list` sets `pending: true` when argv[3] is exactly `--pending`, and every other command carries `rest = argv.slice(3)`. `runCommand` writes every byte of user-visible output through `io.out` / `io.err` only — no `console`, no `process.stdout` — so tests capture output by passing a fake `io` object.

Output formats, owned by src/cli.js and relied on by the end-to-end tests and the README: a pending todo is rendered as `` `[ ] ${id} ${text}` ``; a finished todo is rendered as `` `[x] ${id} ${text}` `` (lowercase letter x, exactly one check-mark character before the closing bracket); `list` prints the single line `No todos.` when the store is empty; `list --pending` prints the single line `No todos.` when nothing is pending; `add` prints `Added <id> <text>`; `done` prints `Done <id>`; `remove` prints `Removed <id>`; errors are written to stderr as `Error: <message>` followed by a newline with exit code 1; `help` (bare `todo`, `todo --help` or `todo help`) prints the multi-line usage block listing the commands add, list [--pending], done, remove and the store path.
